One clip each, with how the family fared

The bar under each title is the acceptance rate for that behaviour. The clip is the ego camera — the observation a policy would actually be trained on, which is why it is the one worth inspecting. Prefer an accepted clip where one exists.

What a single episode looks like from inside

Before you trust any of this

Known wrong, so you do not have to find it

No accepted episode touches the scene. Lateral scene contact is 0.000 N across all 133 of them; the 18 episodes that did touch something were all rejected for it. The clutter is built around the corridor the robot actually walked, so this is traversability by construction rather than by luck — and it is the one guarantee here that does not weaken as behaviours diversify.

The dominant rejection is excessive_self_contact, causing 15 of 24 rejections. Gates that measure agreement with the Kimodo reference no longer decide acceptance for scene-around-motion episodes: the room is built around the corridor the robot executed, so the reference was a means of producing behaviour rather than the label. Departures from it are recorded as diagnostics.

The third-person camera clips inside furniture in dense scenes, blanking part of the frame, and the overhead camera renders blank. Both are review-tooling defects, not data defects; the overhead one is unfixed and was reverted rather than shipped with a speculative fix.

1 behaviour family(ies) accept nothing at all: squat to pick up (0 of 3). For the squat that is a robot limit rather than a tracker failure -- the G1's waist pitch cannot fold as far as the reference asks, so the joint clamps and the thigh ends up through the pelvis.

Half the families are too small to quote. 11 of 13 have fewer than ten episodes, where a 100% rate means very little. Treat per-family percentages here as provisional until the quota floor is met.
